messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired — service="inference-frontend" severity=critical; reason=p99 latency > 1200ms for 10m. PD ID PD-89321. Region: us-west1. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-tail-latency
pagerduty-bot: Paging on-call: @ajay (primary). Please acknowledge: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-89321 :rotating_light:
ajay: acked — looking into it now. Can someone confirm if this is regional or global?
sarah: seeing similar but smaller bump in us-east. us-west is definitely worse. I'm free to jump in if you want help.
ajay: quick skim of traces shows heavy tail on model inference calls, latencies cluster around model-side batching timeouts and a spike of queued requests. Checking sidecar and autoscaler metrics.
devon: I see a sudden queue length jump on pods servicing model-v2 in us-west1 around 22:01. Possible cold-start wave after a scaling decision. Metrics snapshot: cpu_util ~ 92%, queue_len ~ 1200, kv_cache_miss_rate up 18%.
maria: Customer impact: Alerting shows ~4.7% of external requests hitting > p99 threshold. CS already flagged 2 enterprise customers on slack. No 5xx spike yet.
ajay: running quick mitigation — bumping pool size for model-v2 in us-west by +3 nodes, enabling fast-warmup. Command: `krel scale inference-pool-model-v2 --region us-west1 --replicas +3`
devon: starting canary reroute to model-v1-fallback for new requests under latency-sensitive route. Route ID: reroute-ccf1. Will drain after stability.
incident-bot: Note: automatic autoscaler suppressed further scale-downs due to surge; suppression window extended by 10m.
ajay: also disabling aggressive batching on that pool to avoid large waiting batches; applying config patch:
```
PATCH /api/configs/batching
{
  "pool": "model-v2-us-west1",
  "max_batch_wait_ms": 5
}
```
sarah: good call, smaller batches reduce tail at cost of tokens/sec. Keep an eye on cost but prioritize SLO for now.
maria: logged customer-impacted sessions and notified SRE runbook. CS update draft: "We are mitigating elevated inference latency in us-west; some requests may be slower than usual. No errors expected; we are actively scaling and rerouting."
ajay: pagerduty: PD status -> acknowledged; escalating to L2 per runbook (oncall escalation).
pagerduty-bot: PD-89321 escalated to L2 (sre-oncall).
devon: applying kvcache warmup for hot prefixes from recent traffic: `kvcache-warm --pool model-v2-us-west1 --keys-file /tmp/hot_keys.txt`
ajay: quick trace after initial actions — p99 dropped from ~1450ms to ~720ms within two minutes. Queue length trending down to ~300.
sarah: nice. Any sign of underlying infra fault or was this workload surge + batching + coldstarts?
ajay: early signal points to coordinated traffic spike + batching timer misalignment + slow node join during autoscale. Not hardware.
maria: continuing CS comms. Also flagging for post-incident review: clearer autoscaler hysteresis and kvcache pre-warm policies.
ajay: will keep monitoring for 15m; if stable will start rollback of aggressive changes (re-enable batching with higher concurrency). Handoff to @sarah at 22:15 for observation window.
sarah: taking over monitoring at 22:15 — noted. If p99 stays under 800ms for 10m we'll close PD and file a follow-up. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: PD-89321 status -> monitoring.
incident-bot: Incident notes appended to PD: actions - scaled +3 nodes, disabled aggressive batching, canary reroute to v1-fallback, cache warmup executed.
ajay: final check (22:09): p95 ~ 110ms, p99 ~ 610ms, error rate stable. No customer-facing degradations remain reported.
maria: CS updated and customers acknowledged. I'll create follow-up ticket for runbook tweaks and postmortem.
sarah: thanks team — leaving notes and will create the post-incident page. Handoff complete.
ajay: thanks all — marking this thread for postmortem input. Feel free to DM if you have logs to attach. :white_check_mark:
